changes: Separate the visible transcript from the history used for sends, retries and Combined recovery. Ordinary chat opens page the latest 40 turns and message links retain their anchor.

Use compiler-produced JVM method descriptors, source lines and call sites for repository impact and test discovery. Keep language-level lexical matches identifiable when a matching build artifact is unavailable.
Replay redacted GitHub reads on an exact revision and compare routing policies by verified requirements, repeat reads, elapsed time and available token receipts.
Choose GitHub evidence sources using unmet criteria, measured yields, permissions and the validity of cached source ranges.
Carry source revision, blob and line ranges to the final provider request, record omission or partial delivery, and link source-backed conclusions to independently observed evidence where available.
Join changed Android line and branch coverage with fresh named JUnit outcomes. The PR gate checks reviewed behavior contracts and retains a change-by-change report.
Benchmark repository-map reuse across chats, branch movement, account switches and eviction using the production cache and repeatable fixtures.
Offer verified retention as a dispatch requirement for private chats while preserving profile selection, on-device inference and local masking.
Set recognition and synthesis languages independently and retain observed local voice and backend evidence separately from requested accelerator placement.
Preserve the PR’s LiteRT speech and Adreno FP32 changes, improve GitHub search and saved-page continuation, and reduce Gateway job and saved-chat lookup costs.
Recover interrupted provider streams, CI job selectors, saved source pages and transient GitHub reads. Preserve exact fixture approvals, cleanup reserves and evidence scope during task verification.

Prepare optimized Kokoro GPU and Snapdragon 8 Elite vocoders locally from the standard first-launch pack. Start word highlights on the first playable PCM, preserve the voice across backends, and recover from early accelerator failures without repeating speech.

Use the measured size when restoring a saved page, distinguish a cancelled queue from an uncertain dispatch, and allow an ongoing lower-effort GitHub turn to finish when its intelligence setting is raised.

Retain issued GitHub saved pages across temporary tool instances, preserve original readback evidence during reconciliation, avoid duplicate reports for archived failures, and guide CI job discovery during continuation.
Honor an OpenAI Responses terminal receipt even when the stream subsequently raises a cleanup error.
Verify the two public routing requirement digests in the credential history scan across PR merge revisions, with controls for different values, paths, fields and adjacent content.
Stream the complete compiled JVM call index to a temporary file and publish it atomically within a shared 128 MiB decoded bound, retaining the 32 MiB Gateway archive bound and revision checks.

Rebuild GitHub chat setup, task routing, context selection and progress around the selected repository. Fresh profiles use adaptive effort. Direct lookups start with the relevant read, and the chat header keeps branch and activity visible.
limitations: The SDK exposes no per-kernel processor or arithmetic receipt. The 17-partition SM8750 vocoder is host-compiled and requires physical playback, CPU-reference validation and listening tests. Hexagon accepts floating-point partitions at hardware-supported reduced precision.
Unified Reliability v2 is not complete; this scoped release does not mark the broader milestone or unexecuted scenarios as passed.
Physical Android performance, selected-provider behavior and the user's Windows/Gateway network require live device/service qualification. Automated fixtures do not establish those conditions.

External provider rate limits, account credit balances and unavailable servers require their service or configuration conditions to recover; client changes improve classification, safe continuation and diagnostic evidence.

The recorded QNN graph qualification used the official x86 HTP emulator and observed 39 QNN kernels per tested token shape with remaining graph work on CPU. It did not run on physical Adreno GPU or Hexagon NPU hardware and does not establish on-device acceleration, speedup, thermal behavior or battery use.

Kokoro GPU/NPU execution is partial and device/model/runtime dependent. A registered provider or selected hardware label is not proof of accelerator execution; failed qualification or stale measurements retain CPU until a successful device recheck.

Physical audio-route latency, caption alignment, interruption recovery, long-reply continuity and frame/memory behavior still require speaker, wired and Bluetooth replay on the target phone. Bounded buffering cannot guarantee uninterrupted speech when synthesis remains slower than playback.
Gateway CUDA remains optional and requires a reachable, compatible configured Gateway. Local fixtures do not qualify the selected desktop GPU, account, network or live service.

The host QNN probes verify finite nonzero PCM and timing from the same inference, not waveform or perceptual equivalence. The 83-token probe differs from its CPU reference by 50 ms of total predicted duration; the recorded host emulator uses ORT 1.28.0 while native/JNI validation uses the pinned application ORT 1.28.2.

Phone repository relationships are bounded lexical candidates, not compiler-resolved references or executed-test evidence. Unscanned, unsupported, generated and dynamic code can leave relationships unknown; current GitHub authorization and connectivity are required, and physical-phone performance remains unqualified.

Optional coding agents require installed pinned runtimes, explicit host configuration and compatible provider accounts. Protocol fixtures and host builds do not qualify paid provider execution, installed SDK compatibility, model quality or remote cancellation when the provider does not support it.

Older provider-wait checkpoints without protected replay-content and result-semantics evidence require recovery review; completed work is retained and writes are not automatically repeated to manufacture missing proof.

Engineering comparisons apply only to their frozen suite, evidence lane, task families, budgets and selected profile settings. Incomplete, incomparable or statistically inconclusive results do not establish a universally superior model.

The Python coding pack uses a bounded Python interpreter. Repository-native fixtures execute Kotlin/JVM, SQLite and declared workflow semantics; they do not claim Android Compose instrumentation, Room processor coverage or arbitrary production-repository correctness.

Live GitHub benchmarking requires an explicitly authorized disposable repository, immutable fixture base, appropriate account permissions and the declared runtime. Direct phone execution needs a provisioned Actions fixture bank; repository-native Actions additionally needs the prepared self-hosted runner and pinned image.

Generation identity is an authenticated client observation, not independent proof of the provider's internal model identity. Missing or ambiguous token usage, price, retry or settings evidence remains unknown; external CI and service charges are not inferred.

The separate native cancellation/failure/reuse regression uses pinned application ORT 1.28.2 with the official QNN 2.7 host emulator, explicit host device/STL ports and a deterministic fault after real kernel execution. It establishes session/profile lifecycle behavior; physical GPU/HTP performance and Android packaging remain separate qualifications.

Prepared Android compilation requires at least 8,960 MiB of observed RAM/cgroup headroom for its fixed 6 GiB heap. The existing 8 GiB container default is refused; an operator must explicitly approve sufficient resources. The preflight does not reserve future memory.
No device speedup is claimed for the Markdown or index changes. The added UI fixture and deterministic runtime regressions do not replace measurement on the target phone.

The historical HTTP 422 commit lookup and NoSuchElementException reports did not retain enough evidence to prove their original root causes. This release preserves their bounded diagnostic capture and regression coverage; it does not declare those incidents reproduced or fixed.

Privacy masking protects detected spans and explicit private terms; final-wire evidence checks known protected values in supported text surfaces. Synthetic phrase preservation and CPU timing do not qualify arbitrary private-data detection, live provider answer quality, provider retention or GPU/NPU execution. Full forensic diagnostic export deliberately includes more content after explicit preview; private memory indexing still requires an authorized ready local model.

The ordinary modal exception is limited to positively classified I may request wording with a discovered May surname and an exact user or history surface. Other ambiguous language and system-prefix collisions remain fail-closed; general semantic name disambiguation is not claimed.

CPU-reference speech checks establish bounded numerical consistency, not perceptual equivalence or physical GPU/NPU speedup. Capture-local reuse avoids repeated redaction only; device startup, database hydration and export latency still require measurement.
MediaPipe delegate selection is a request; the SDK exposes no executed-kernel receipt or CPU thread control. Its GPU option is excluded from the native ONNX CPU/GPU/NPU verified ranking.

MediaPipe word timestamps are estimated. Host checkpoint smoke and Android runtime compatibility do not establish target-phone speed, perceptual speech quality, acoustic word alignment, battery savings or physical GPU execution.
Gateway binary streaming transports the current CUDA model's completed neural phrase. It removes Base64 delivery overhead but does not claim incremental CUDA neural generation.

Production accelerator admission establishes numerical consistency on the fixed representative CPU-reference workload. It does not prove perceptual equivalence or correctness for every future utterance; native per-phrase validation remains required.

Privacy provider comparison uses at most four scored fictional pairs after two warmups. It reports deterministic fixture criteria, not general semantic quality or arbitrary-input detection recall. Missing backend/cap observations, mismatched or incomplete pairs, and strict private routes with unverified sampling parity are excluded from timing summaries; small nearest-rank samples do not establish a stable p95 distribution, causal privacy overhead or provider retention. Live selected-provider performance is not measured by implementation tests.

Streaming speech delivery feedback has bounded-state and ordinary-worker regression coverage; those controls do not identify every device-specific cause of audible stutter or establish perceptual playback improvement. Physical voice/route measurements remain separate.

Silent inference and audible playback are separate speech measurements. Native first PCM records a completed chunk and SDK first PCM records a delivered callback; presented audio uses the production AudioTrack timestamp or playback head. Caption checks measure observed word coverage and clock consistency. Acoustic speaker latency, perceptual word alignment, battery energy and hardware utilization percentages remain unmeasured. GPU/NPU results require compatible real hardware and actual accelerator execution; unsupported or failed trials retain their observed status.

The added engine benchmark measures structural PCM, callback delivery and playback behavior. It does not establish cross-engine intelligibility, perceptual equivalence, acoustic latency, energy savings or an automatic engine winner. The supplied 631bad14 phone logs are baseline observations, not verification of these changes.

Final-request refusal diagnostics report only the four observed typed outcomes from current validation. Missing historical receipt causes remain unknown; prior accepted or uncertain work cannot be reduced to unsent. Source and receiver data checks do not replace ordinary hosted composed runtime qualification or private capture/approval policy.

Optional battery-counter decreases describe whole-device observations, not energy attributable to a speech engine, wattage or savings; missing, coarse, interrupted or charging observations remain explicit. Silent CPU warmup and strict zero-clipping controls do not prove target-phone speed or acoustic continuity. The earlier context-export failure remains historical evidence. The paired QNN 2.8/QAIRT 2.52 mixed-graph host test now passes embedded-context save/reload; this does not qualify the full Kokoro graph, physical-phone cache performance or arbitrary-utterance GPU/NPU correctness.

The runtime rebuild, original-weight tools, incremental-input controls and sustained qualification are implemented with scoped source/host checks and required Android release gates. Full Kokoro context save/load/corruption recovery passes with the pinned x86 HTP host emulator. These observations do not establish physical-phone cache performance, perceptual speech quality, lower battery use or a measured GPU/NPU speedup; fresh device reports are required.

Pronunciation checks verify readable text, source-aligned captions and frontend token compatibility; they do not establish phone acoustic accuracy, general multilingual support or sentence-dependent homograph correctness.

Production GitHub intelligence scores and comparisons with ChatGPT or Codex require matched live qualification runs. Proposed performance targets remain unmeasured without the corresponding observations.

Recovery reads selected by a helper are unavailable when the primary profile uses LiteRt-LM. Saved recovery-read choices remain visible but inactive; advice-only recovery keeps its existing eligibility rules.

GPU and HTP speech qualification and listening quality require measured results on the target phone. A rejected tensor comparison, a cache hit or an instrumented model capture alone does not qualify an accelerator.

Native-product and reader-preference comparisons require independently collected observations. This release supplies the evaluation workflows and makes no measured claim of superiority over Codex or Claude Code.

The earlier 253,719,782-byte signed universal APK remains over the 230 MiB limit by 12,547,302 bytes. The sparse regression is a historical negative fixture, not a final artifact measurement; current signed packaging and all publication gates remain required.
Physical ROG Phone 9 Pro playback and three-listener pronunciation comparisons remain unmeasured for the revised planner. Native FP32 processor preference requires device-specific qualification.
The repository-map benchmark uses simulated GitHub transport. A host measurement or requested speech delegate does not establish live handset latency or physical accelerator placement.
